newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls on liquidity, swaps down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls on liquidity, swaps down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah eased against the dollar in early trading on Tuesday on the back of ample rupiah liquidity as short-dated swaps were seen falling further, dealers said.
One senior director with a U.S. bank in Jakarta said the falls in the rupiah short-dated swap rates were due to rising onshore dollar lending rates because of quarter and half-year end demand.
"As a result dealers who need to borrow US dollars overnight and tom/next have been generating them by buying and selling US dollars through the short-date swap market," the director said.
Overnight swap was last at par/0.05 points from an opening of 0.15/0.30 while tom/next was down at 0.02/0.05 points against 0.10/0.20 at the opening.

One-month swaps also fell to 10.75/11.25 from an opening of 11.00/12.00, two fell to 23.75/24.50 from 25.50/26.50, three to 37.00/38.00 from 39.50/40.50 and six to 78.50/80.00 from 81.00/82.50 points.
Another dealer said the weak spot rupiah rate was attributed to sustained rupiah liquidity.
Spot rupiah was at 2,432.50/33.00 at 0330 GMT against an opening of 2,431.80/32.30.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were last at 2,432.40/32.90 and 2,433.00/33.50, respectively.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, raised its intervention band by one point to 2,426/2,618 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,426/2,474 late on Monday.
